hero.accent: নাম আলাদা, ওষুধ একই — প্যারাসিটামল, দুইবার।
hero.body: Elderly Bangladeshis collect medicines from a hospital doctor, a village doctor and the local drug shop, under thousands of brand names, and nobody looks at the whole shelf. OushodhSathi reads every strip in the house, catches duplicates and dangerous combinations, and a pharmacist or doctor confirms every finding before the family sees it, in simple Bangla.
hero.demoNote: The demo opens the invented household of Rahima Begum, 68, Cumilla.

how.title: How it works
how.body: A family member photographs every strip, box and prescription. Six steps later the family has one clinician-checked list and a passport to carry to every doctor visit.

s1.title: Photograph
s1.body: Every strip, box and prescription in the house, cut strips included.

s2.title: Read
s2.body: A vision model turns photos into typed items: brand, strength, expiry, confidence.

s3.title: Match
s3.body: Each Bangladeshi brand maps to its generic. Unknown brands are searched on Bangladeshi medicine sites and marked unverified.

s4.title: Check
s4.body: A deterministic engine flags duplicates, same-class pairs, interactions, Beers 65+ drugs and expired strips.

s5.title: Confirm
s5.body: A pharmacist or doctor confirms or dismisses each finding, with a note, in under 30 seconds.

s6.title: Understand
s6.body: The family sees only confirmed findings in plain Bangla, a weekly report and a printable passport.

safe.title: AI for perception. Rules and humans for judgement.
safe.accent: এআই পড়ে, নিয়ম আর মানুষ বিচার করে।
safe.body: A vision model is good at reading a cut strip under a tube light. It is not who should decide that a 68-year-old is taking paracetamol twice. So it doesn’t.

r1.title: Rules make every finding.
r1.body: A deterministic engine flags duplicates, interactions, drugs risky after 65 and expired strips. Language models never create, remove or grade a finding.

r2.title: A clinician confirms before the family sees it.
r2.body: Findings start as pending. The API only ever returns confirmed findings to the family, and a test enforces it.

r3.title: We never tell anyone to stop a medicine.
r3.body: Explanations are checked for doses and stop-words, and always end: ডাক্তারের সাথে কথা না বলে কোনো ওষুধ বন্ধ বা পরিবর্তন করবেন না।

r4.title: Uncertain readings are marked.
r4.body: Anything read with under 75% confidence, or matched from the web, is shown as needing a human check.

r5.title: Names stay out of models.
r5.body: Only medicine photos and medicine names reach a model. Patient names and phone numbers never do.

r6.title: Photos are not kept.
r6.body: Photos are read in memory and discarded; the family sees a thumbnail once.

docs.title: OushodhSathi, in depth
docs.accent: ওষুধসাথী — পিচ, হোয়াইটপেপার ও সিস্টেম ড্যাশবোর্ড
docs.intro: The live pitch, technical whitepaper and system dashboard for the International AI Builders Congress 2026 (HealthSphere AI → ChronicCare AI). Every number on this page is either cited, read live from the running system, or labelled as demo data.

problem.body: An elderly patient with high blood pressure or diabetes in Bangladesh often collects medicines from three places: a hospital outpatient doctor, a village doctor, and the local drug shop. Each sees only their own prescription. The same molecule is sold under many brand names, so a family cannot tell that Napa and Ace are both paracetamol, or that two doctors have each started amlodipine.
problem.l1: Hypertension is now the most common illness in Bangladesh, at 78.28 per 1,000 people (BBS Health and Morbidity Status Survey 2025, as reported by <bss>BSS</bss> and <ds>The Daily Star</ds>).
problem.l2: Only 11% of people with hypertension had their blood pressure controlled below 140/90, a background figure in the <heart>WHO-HEARTS evaluation in Bangladesh (Heart, 2024)</heart>.
problem.l3: In a small 2011 study of 35 geriatric outpatients at a private hospital, 69% were prescribed five or more medicines (<trend>Trends of prescribing for out-door geriatric patients</trend>).

solution.body: A family member photographs every strip, box and prescription. A vision model reads the photos into a typed list; each brand is mapped to its generic; a deterministic rules engine flags duplicates, same-class pairs, interactions, drugs risky after 65 (AGS Beers Criteria) and expired strips; a pharmacist or doctor confirms every flag; and only then does the family see a plain-Bangla explanation, a weekly report and a printable medicine passport with a QR code.

ai.body: One router (backend/app/llm_router.py) talks to every model through OpenAI-compatible APIs, falls through on 429, 5xx and timeouts, and caches every response in SQLite by a SHA-256 of task, model and messages. The shelf agent is built with Pydantic-AI and may call three tools: match_brand, lookup_unknown_brand and a read-only check_medicines. It cannot write flags.

r1.model: Free OpenRouter vision model (auto-picked: price 0, image input, largest context), then NARAROUTER → EXPLAB → AGENTROUTER
r1.why: Cut strips, glare and Bangla text need a vision model; free models keep it affordable
r1.guard: Typed Pydantic output, one retry, then needs-review; confidence < 0.75 always shown for a human check

r2.model: Tavily search on medex.com.bd, arogga.com, medeasy.health + text model; Perplexity Agent API fallback
r2.why: Bangladesh has tens of thousands of brands; the seed table cannot hold them all
r2.guard: Model must cite a numbered result; stored as web_unverified with the source URL; failures never cached

r3.model: Ollama qwen2.5:3b locally first, cloud fallback
r3.why: Private and free when run locally
r3.guard: Only for confirmed flags; dose and stop-word filter; fixed template fallback; fixed safety sentence

r4.model: No model. Deterministic rules in backend/app/rules.py
r4.why: Judgement must be repeatable and auditable
r4.guard: Pure functions with tests; a clinician confirms every flag

ai.prompts: Prompts are versioned files in backend/app/prompts/ (extract_strip.v1, brand_lookup.v1, explain_bn.v1). Changing a prompt means a new version file and a new eval run.

safety.s1: Safety flags come only from the deterministic rules engine. Models never create, remove or change the severity of a flag.
safety.s2: Flags start as pending review. The family view of the API returns only confirmed flags, and a test enforces it.
safety.s3: No text tells a patient to stop, start or change a medicine or a dose.
safety.s4: Readings below 0.75 confidence and web-found brand matches are always marked for human confirmation.
safety.s5: Patient names and phone numbers are never sent to a model, only medicine photos and medicine names.
safety.s6: Photos are processed in memory and not stored after extraction.
safety.pdpo: These follow the data-minimisation and purpose-limitation principles of Bangladesh’s Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025 (PDPO). OushodhSathi is a research prototype, not a medical device, and makes no compliance claim.

models.title: AI models
models.intro: OushodhSathi tries these models in order. If one is busy, out of credits or withdrawn, the next one answers automatically — you never have to switch by hand.
models.safety: Whichever model answers, it only reads photos, finds brands and words explanations. Safety findings always come from fixed rules and a clinician.

vision.title: Reading photos
vision.desc: Turns photos of strips, boxes and prescriptions into a medicine list.

text.title: Looking up unknown brands
text.desc: Reads Bangladeshi medicine-site results to find a brand’s generic. Results are always marked unverified.

explain_bn.title: Bangla explanations
explain_bn.desc: Written only after a clinician confirms a finding. Your own computer (Ollama) is tried first when it is running.

models.templates: If no model answers, fixed, pre-checked Bangla templates are used.
models.fixedNote: The order for explanations is fixed: on your computer first, then the cloud.
models.checking: Checking which free models answer… the first time can take a few seconds.
